title: The 4 primary roles of AI in automated workflows
summary: Use this practical framework—based on Zapier's AI Workflow Index—to help you decide where AI actually belongs in your organizational workflows.
body_text: My in-laws have wired every light in their house to Alexa. But no one can ever remember if they're sitting in the "living room" or the "family room," so three commands and one accidental playlist later, someone always ends up just leaning over and hitting the light switch. A lot of AI workflows are built the same way—for example, someone calls a model to check if a number is above a threshold. This is something a conditional rule has handled since the early days of Excel. There's no judgment to make or language to interpret. It's just a number, and you either act on it or you don't. And yet the instinct to reach for AI anyway is everywhere. That overhead adds up: according to Zapier's AI Workflow Index , workflows that reserve AI for reasoning steps cost 71% less to run than workflows that route every step through a model. Here's a practical framework to help you decide where AI actually belongs in your workflow. Table of contents: The 4 primary roles of AI in automated workflows How to tell where AI belongs in your workflow Where to start adding AI into your workflows (and how to grow from there) Build AI workflows on Zapier The 4 primary roles of AI in automated workflows Zapier's AI Workflow Index analyzed how the top 25% of mid-market and enterprise companies—ranked by AI workflow adoption—actually put AI to work . Across all of them, AI tended to play one of four specific roles. Communicator What AI does in this role: Writes for people The Communicator is the most common AI role in automating workflows by a wide margin: 84% of leading adopters run it. AI's role here is to draft something (for example, summary emails and Slack digests) and send the output to a human—whether that's a teammate reviewing it or a customer receiving it directly. Clerk What AI does in this role : Extracts information and updates records The Clerk is the second most common role, used by 79% of the companies in the index. AI reads unstructured input—for example, a call transcript, an incoming support ticket, or a form submission—and turns it into structured fields in whatever system your team already uses to track things. Analyst What AI does in this role : Makes decisions This role accounts for 44% of all AI workflow runs (and 76% of those happen outside business hours). AI produces a judgment, like a score or a yes/no call, and a downstream step acts on it directly. Coordinator What AI does in this role : Creates tasks The Coordinator shows up in about a quarter of the companies studied, making it the least common of the four. In this role, AI initiates work, taking an inbound signal and turning it into a tracked task or ticket in your team's project management system. How to tell where AI belongs in your workflow The easiest way to identify the right role is to start with who or what receives AI's output. If the output goes to a person , the role is either the Communicator or the Clerk. The way to tell which path to follow comes down to form: the Communicator produces text (for example, a summary, a draft, or a digest), while the Clerk pulls structured fields out of unstructured input and writes them into a system. Either way, a human sees the output before anything acts on it. If the output goes directly to a system or rule , the path depends on whether a human reviews it first . If someone reviews the output before it triggers anything, you're still in Communicator or Clerk territory. If it acts directly (no review step), that's the Analyst or Coordinator. Where to start adding AI into your workflows (and how to grow from there) Before you start building, decide which steps in that workflow actually need AI. Even among leading adopters, only 18% of steps in an AI workflow are actually AI steps. The rest run on rules, logic, and conventional automation. If a step doesn't require judgment or language interpretation, a conditional rule will handle it faster and cheaper. Once you know you need AI, think about what role it's playing. Most organizations (79%) build the Communicator or Clerk first because they're lower stakes. A person sees the output before anything acts on it, so if AI gets something wrong, a human has a chance to catch and correct it. If you're starting from scratch, find a workflow where someone is currently writing something by hand based on inputs they receive, or manually entering data from an unstructured source. Build there first. Once you have a baseline for how AI performs in your workflows, then layer in the Analyst or Coordinator. When you're ready to combine roles, sequence them. Pick a starting role, define what its output looks like, then ask whether a second role naturally picks up from there. If the answer is yes, you have a clean chain. If you can't define where one role ends and the next begins, treat them as separate workflows. Here's an example of what that sequencing looks like in practice: After a sales call ends, AI analyzes the transcript, extracts deal-relevant fields, and adds it to the CRM (Clerk). A conditional rule then checks whether the deal size clears a threshold (no AI needed). If it does, a second AI step scores the lead against fit criteria and returns a routing decision (Analyst). So one role's output becomes the next role's input. Build AI workflows on Zapier The more AI connects to your business tools, the more you need a single place controlling what it can access. That's what Zapier does, letting you securely connect to 9,000+ apps with OAuth-managed connections and granular permissions. And you can build from wherever you work. Describe what you want to create, and Zapier's AI assistant will configure the workflow for you, adding AI only where it's needed. Or you can install Zapier MCP and get ChatGPT, Claude, or another AI assistant to take action without leaving your chat window. However you build, the access model stays the same: you decide which apps and actions your agent can touch, and your IT team can revoke access from one place if something changes. title: Med Spa Reputation Management: HIPAA-Safe Review Replies
summary: In August 2026, active reputation management helps med spas earn more reviews, rank higher locally, and convert prospective clients into booked appointments.
body_text: Why Reputation Management Is Non-Negotiable for Med Spas Prospective clients research med spas extensively before booking, and most of that research happens online. 83% of patients check online reviews before selecting a healthcare provider, and med spas face the same scrutiny. A single wave of negative reviews or an unmonitored social profile can send potential clients straight to a competitor. The stakes are higher in elective care med spas because clients are choosing to spend discretionary income on visible, personal treatments. Trust has to be earned before they ever walk through the door. The Anatomy of a Strong Google Business Profile Your Google Business Profile (GBP) is often the first thing a prospective patient sees before visiting your website. A complete, well-maintained profile builds immediate credibility and directly influences whether someone books a consultation. There are several elements that separate a high-performing GBP from a neglected one: Keep your business name, location, phone number, and hours accurate and consistent across every directory listing you have. Staying current with new med spa laws also shapes how you present your practice publicly. Upload high-quality photos of your space, staff, and treatments regularly, since profiles with photos tend to receive more direction requests and clicks. Write a practice description that reflects the services you offer and the patient experience you provide. Use the Q&A section proactively by posting and answering common questions before patients need to ask them. Respond to every review, positive or negative, to show prospective patients that your practice is attentive and accountable. Building a Consistent Flow of Patient Reviews Reviews are the backbone of med spa reputation management. Practices that actively request feedback collect reviews at 7x the rate of those that wait passively. A simple post-appointment patient message asking patients to share their experience can meaningfully shift your review volume over weeks, not months. Timing matters. Asking within 24 hours of a visit, when satisfaction is highest, produces the strongest response rates. Rotating your ask across Google, RealSelf, and Yelp keeps your profile healthy across the directories prospective patients check most. Setting Up a Sustainable Review Cadence Make review requests part of your checkout workflow so no patient slips through without a prompt, and pair this with efforts to reduce med spa no-shows that would otherwise leave gaps in your schedule. Personalize the message by referencing the specific service received to increase open rates. Follow up once if there is no response, but avoid sending multiple reminders that feel pushy. Responding to Reviews in a HIPAA-Compliant Way Responding to reviews is one of the trickiest parts of med spa reputation management. HIPAA prohibits confirming whether someone is a patient, which means you cannot reference treatments, outcomes, or appointment details in any public reply. The safest approach is to keep responses general and empathetic. Thank the reviewer, invite them to continue the conversation privately, and avoid any language that acknowledges a clinical relationship. What to Avoid in Public Responses Never confirm or deny that the reviewer visited your practice, as doing so can constitute a HIPAA violation. Skip any mention of procedures, results, or scheduling history, even when a negative review feels factually wrong. Resist the urge to over-explain or defend, since lengthy responses often draw more attention to the complaint. Handling Negative Reviews Without Escalating Them Negative reviews sting, but your response matters more than the review itself. Prospective patients read how you handle criticism just as closely as they read the complaint. A measured, professional reply can actually build trust. A few principles to follow: Respond promptly but not reactively. Acknowledge the experience within 24 to 48 hours without admitting liability or arguing the facts publicly. Take the conversation offline. Invite the reviewer to call or email your practice manager so the issue can be resolved privately, and make it easy to rebook with automated calendar scheduling . Stay HIPAA-compliant. Never confirm or deny that someone is a patient, and avoid referencing any treatment details in your reply. Flag genuinely fake reviews. Most review sites have a removal process for reviews that violate their content policies. Where Else Patients Research Med Spas Patients rarely stop at Google reviews. They check RealSelf for before-and-after photos, browse Instagram to gauge aesthetic consistency, and scan Yelp for candid feedback. Some visit the Better Business Bureau or Healthgrades before booking a consultation. Each of these touchpoints shapes perception before a patient ever contacts your front desk. Platform Primary Use for Patients What Matters Most Best For Med Spas RealSelf Before-and-after research, peer comparisons Visual proof and community reviews over star ratings Cosmetic and aesthetic procedure credibility Instagram Gauging aesthetic style and consistency Content quality and posting consistency Showcasing results as a living portfolio Yelp Candid feedback, second opinion beyond Google Candid, unfiltered patient sentiment Higher-cost procedure research Healthgrades Provider credibility and patient feedback Clinical trust signals Patients seeking a second opinion before booking Google Business Profile First stop in local search research Star rating, review volume, and profile completeness Local map pack visibility and click-through rates How Reputation Directly Drives Local Search Rankings Your online reputation directly and measurably affects how Google ranks your med spa in local search results. Google's local ranking algorithm weighs three core factors: relevance, distance, and prominence. Reputation signals, particularly review volume, recency, and star ratings, feed directly into prominence. Practices with a higher volume of recent, high-rated reviews consistently outrank competitors in the local map pack. For med spas, where prospective clients are making deeply personal decisions, this visibility gap translates into real differences in appointment volume. Why Review Signals Matter to Google Google interprets consistent review activity as a signal that a business is active, trustworthy, and worth surfacing. Key signals include: Star rating averages, where anything below 4.0 tends to hurt click-through rates meaningfully Review velocity, since a steady stream of new reviews signals ongoing patient satisfaction instead of a one-time burst Keyword-rich review content, which helps Google match your listing to relevant search queries like "botox near me" or "laser treatment [city]" Using Social Media to Reinforce Your Reputation Social media gives med spas a direct channel to shape how prospective clients perceive them before a first appointment is ever booked. Consistent posting of before-and-after results, provider credentials, and patient testimonials builds credibility over time far more reliably than sporadic bursts of content. Engagement matters as much as publishing frequency. Responding to comments, answering DMs promptly, and acknowledging tagged posts signals to your audience that real people are behind the brand, especially when every patient record is organized in one place. Ignoring social interactions, even positive ones, quietly erodes the trust you are working to build elsewhere. Tie your social presence back to review generation by occasionally prompting satisfied followers to share their experience on Google or RealSelf, and use practice analytics to track which channels drive the most bookings. How Decoda Fits Into Your Reputation Management Stack Decoda is built for independent elective-care practices that need patient communication and reputation management working together in one place. The AI Front Desk handles inbound inquiries and follow-ups automatically, so review requests go out at the right moment in the patient journey without requiring manual effort from your front desk team. Ask Decoda lets you surface patient sentiment trends across your practice without digging through spreadsheets. For med spa owners who want their reputation strategy tied directly to their intake and retention workflows, Decoda connects those pieces natively, where most standalone review tools leave gaps. Final Thoughts on Reputation Management for Med Spas Your online reputation is the first conversation you have with a prospective client, and it happens before you know they're looking. Getting the details right, from your Google Business Profile to how you respond to a tough review, builds the kind of trust that converts browsers into booked appointments. None of this requires a massive overhaul, just consistent habits across the right touchpoints. Book a short intro call if you want to see how Decoda fits into that process. Frequently Asked Questions How do you respond to negative Google reviews at a med spa without violating HIPAA? Keep your response general and empathetic — thank the reviewer, acknowledge their experience without confirming they are a patient, and invite them to continue the conversation privately by phone or email. Never reference treatments, appointment history, or outcomes in a public reply, even when the review feels factually inaccurate. What actually moves a med spa up in Google's local map pack rankings? Review volume, recency, and star ratings feed directly into the prominence factor Google uses for local rankings. Practices with a steady stream of recent, high-rated reviews consistently outrank competitors in local search, regardless of physical proximity to the searcher — so a consistent review cadence matters more than a one-time burst. Best way to collect more patient reviews for a med spa without annoying people? Ask within 24 hours of the appointment when satisfaction is at its peak, reference the specific service in your message to increase open rates, and follow up once if there is no response. Rotating your request across Google, RealSelf, and Yelp keeps all three profiles active without overwhelming any single channel. How do I tie review requests directly into my patient checkout workflow instead of managing them manually? Automating review requests at the right moment in the patient journey removes the dependency on front desk staff remembering to send them. Decoda's AI Front Desk handles post-appointment follow-ups automatically, so requests go out consistently without manual effort — connecting your intake and retention workflow to your med spa reputation management in one place rather than through a separate standalone tool. Does responding to every review actually affect how prospective patients perceive a med spa? Yes — prospective patients read how you handle criticism just as closely as they read the complaint itself. A measured, professional reply to a negative review can build trust where a non-response, or an over-defensive one, signals that the practice may be difficult to work with after something goes wrong. Can a med spa prevent a negative review from going public before it reaches Google? No review gating tool can stop a patient from posting directly on Google, and attempting to filter reviews before they go public violates Google's review policies. The more effective approach is building enough review volume that individual negative reviews have minimal weight on your overall star rating, while responding professionally to every concern that does appear publicly. Can the AI in a practice management system automatically respond to patient Google reviews, including negative ones? Decoda's review management feature supports responding to reviews, though AI-generated automatic responses to negative Google reviews are not yet a live capability as of mid-2026. Responding to negative reviews still requires a staff member to craft the reply, which gives you direct control over HIPAA compliance in every public response. What star rating does a med spa need to maintain to stay competitive in local search? Anything below 4.0 tends to hurt click-through rates in a meaningful way, and most prospective clients filter out practices rated below 4.2 when browsing local search results. Staying above that threshold requires a consistent flow of new reviews, because a handful of older negative reviews can drag down an otherwise healthy average if no fresh positive ones are coming in. How does posting social media content from a practice management system actually work? Decoda includes a content studio that generates SEO-optimized blog posts and supports publishing to Instagram and Facebook directly from the platform, so you are not logging into separate apps to schedule posts. This consolidates your content creation and social publishing into the same system handling your scheduling, communications, and patient records. Should I ask every patient for a review, or only the ones I know had a great experience? Ask every patient who completed an appointment, since selectively requesting reviews from satisfied patients and ignoring others can introduce bias that makes your profile look artificially positive. Platforms like Google explicitly prohibit soliciting reviews only from patients you expect to leave positive feedback, so a consistent ask-everyone approach is both the compliant and more sustainable strategy. How do RealSelf reviews affect a med spa's reputation differently from Google reviews? RealSelf reviews carry significant weight for cosmetic and aesthetic decisions specifically because the audience is actively comparing procedures and outcomes, not just searching for a nearby provider. A strong RealSelf presence with before-and-after content and detailed reviews can influence a prospective client who has already shortlisted your practice and wants visual and peer-verified confirmation before booking a higher-cost treatment. What should go into a Google Business Profile to give a med spa the best chance of ranking in the local map pack? A complete profile includes accurate business name, address, phone number, and hours that match every other directory listing you have, along with high-quality photos of your space and staff uploaded regularly. Beyond the basics, proactively populating the Q&A section with common patient questions and writing a practice description that reflects your actual service menu gives Google more signals to match your listing to relevant searches like 'botox near me' or 'laser treatment' in your city. How do I get patients to leave keyword-rich reviews that help with local SEO without coaching them on what to say? You cannot direct patients to include specific words, but you can prompt them naturally by referencing the service in your follow-up message, such as asking how they felt after their appointment. Patients who respond tend to describe what they experienced in their own words, which often includes the treatment name, your city, and qualitative language that maps to local search queries on its own. How does med spa reputation management change when you have multiple locations? Each location needs its own Google Business Profile, its own review cadence, and its own response workflow because Google ranks locations independently and a strong profile at one location does not carry over to another. The operational challenge is keeping review requests and responses consistent across locations without requiring a separate system for each one, which is where having patient communications and follow-ups running through a single practice management system matters more than it does for a single-location practice. What is the right way to take a negative review conversation offline without making the response look dismissive? Acknowledge the experience briefly in your public reply, express that you want to make it right, and give a specific contact point such as a practice manager's direct email or phone number so the path forward is clear. Keeping the public reply to two or three sentences signals accountability without feeding the complaint more visibility, and resolving it privately removes the incentive for the reviewer to escalate further online.

title: Nanox and Vertec Scientific Enter Exclusive Sales Reseller Agreement for the Commercialization of Nanox.AI Bone Solution (HealthOST) in the United Kingdom
summary: Initial three-year term includes minimum annual license commitments PETACH TIKVA, ISRAEL, August 18 2026 -- Nanox Imaging Ltd. (“ Nanox”, or the “Company” NASDAQ: NNOX), a leader in innovative medical imaging technology, today announced its subsidiary, Nanox AI Ltd.
body_text: Initial three-year term includes minimum annual license commitments PETACH TIKVA, ISRAEL, August 18 2026 -- Nanox Imaging Ltd. (“ Nanox”, or the “Company” NASDAQ: NNOX), a leader in innovative medical imaging technology, today announced its subsidiary, Nanox AI Ltd. (“Nanox AI”) e ntered into a sales reseller agreement with Vertec Scientific L td. (“ Vertec ”) for the commercialization of Nanox.AI b one solution ( HealthOST ) in the United Kingdom. The agreement grants Vertec an exclusive license to market and resell HealthOST in the United Kingdom, subject to Vertec satisfying minimum annual license commitments , over an initial three-year term. Nanox.AI bone solution (HealthOST) is an FDA-cleared and UKCA/ CE-marked AI software solution that analyzes eligible routine CT scans . Nanox.AI bone solution (HealthOST) is an AI-enabled image processing software that provides qualitative and quantitative analysis of the spine from CT images to support clinicians in the evaluation and assessment of musculoskeletal disease of the spine, such as osteoporosis. The software provides vertebral labeling , vertebral height-loss measurements and vertebral bone-attenuation measurements. Since the CT scans analyzed by HealthOST were performed for other clinical indications, no additional imaging, radiation or patient time is required, enabling opportunistic assessment from routine CT scans. HealthOST is seamlessly integrated with existing picture archiving and communication systems (PACS) and can enable timely and appropriate preventive care. In November 2025 , the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) rec omm en d e d Heal thOST , as wel l as a previou s version , Health VC F , among five AI technologies for National Health Service (NHS) use “as options to aid the opportunistic detection of vertebral fragility fractures (VFFs) . ” Vertec is a UK-based provider of DXA and bone health solutions, serving hospitals, clinics, and healthcare providers across the UK. First established in Berkshire in 1979, Vertec has built nearly five decades of experience as one of the UK's leading DXA suppliers, supported by nationwide, OEM-authorized engineering coverage and a team of clinically trained Applications and P roduct S pecialists. Erez Meltzer, Chief Executive Officer and Acting Chairman of Nanox, said: “ This agreement expands the reach of our AI b one so lution into the UK market and reflects our continued momentum in bringing AI-driven bone health assessment to healthcare providers. Vertec Scientific's established presence in DXA and bone health solutions makes them a strong partner to support this rollout across the UK.” K ate O’Reilly , Managing Director of Vertec, added : “We are delighted to bring Health OST to healthcare providers across the UK. Osteoporosis and vertebral fractures too often go undetected until it's too late, and this technology gives clinicians a straightforward way to identify at-risk patients from routine scans , enabling more timely and proactive interventions . We look forward to working with Nanox AI to expand access to this solution across the UK.” About Nanox Nanox (NASDAQ: NNOX) is focused on driving the world's transition to preventive health care by delivering an integrated, end-to-end medical imaging and healthcare services platform. Nanox combines affordable imaging hardware, advanced AI-based solutions, cloud-based software, access to remote radiology, health IT solutions, and a marketplace to enable earlier detection, improved clinical efficiency, and broader access to care. Nanox's vision is to expand the reach of medical imaging both within and beyond traditional hospital settings by providing a seamless solution from scan to interpretation and beyond. By leveraging proprietary digital X-ray technology, AI-driven analytics, and a clinically driven approach, Nanox aims to enhance the efficiency of routine imaging workflows, support early detection of disease, and improve patient outcomes. The Nanox ecosystem includes Nanox.ARC, a cost-effective, 3D multi-source digital tomosynthesis imaging system designed for ease of use and scalability; Nanox.AI, a suite of AI-based algorithms that augment the interpretation of routine CT imaging to identify early signs often associated with chronic disease; Nanox.CLOUD, a cloud-based platform for secure data management, storage, and advanced imaging analytics; Nanox.MARKETPLACE and USARAD Holdings, which provide access to remote radiology and cardiology experts and comprehensive teleradiology services; and Nanox Health IT, which combines deep healthcare IT expertise with leading technology partners to deliver RIS, PACS, AI, dictation, and secure infrastructure solutions that streamline workflows and support safer, more efficient care delivery. www.nanox.vision About Nanox.AI Nanox.AI is the deep-learning medical imaging analytics subsidiary of Nanox. Nanox.AI solutions are developed to target highly prevalent chronic and acute diseases affecting large populations around the world. Leveraging AI, Nanox.AI helps clinicians extract valuable and actionable clinical insights from medical imaging that otherwise may go unnoticed, potentially initiating further medical assessment to establish individual preventative care pathways for patients. For more information, please visit www.nanox.vision/ai. About Vertec Scientific Ltd Now established in the UK for nearly 50 years, Vertec Scientific has earned a reputation for supplying and supporting a wide range of high quality health technology products, accessories and consumables from across the world. This range includes Hologic DXA, mini c-arm systems, mobile x-ray systems, dosimetry, radiotherapy treatment alignment and immobilization devices, including thermoplastics, plus much more. The portfolio is supported by qualified Applications Specialists, Product Specialists and multi-faceted Service Engineers. Vertec’s success is due to its unyielding customer focus and its strategy of only marketing best-in-class products. body_text: Diversified Energy Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results August 05, 2026 4:17 PM EDT Download as PDF Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio Presentation PDF 10-Q HTML PDF XBRL ZIP BIRMINGHAM, Ala., Aug. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Diversified Energy Company ("Diversified", "DEC", or the "Company") (NYSE: DEC, LSE: DEC) is pleased to announce its financial and operational results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026. Operated Development Program: Building on our proven acquisition and asset optimization model, DEC is expanding its value creation strategy through a disciplined one-rig operated development program focused on generating high-return organic cash flow growth from our high-quality, drill-ready inventory in Oklahoma. Shareholder Returns: Diversified’s cash generative, differentiated business model has allowed for year to date returns of ~$136M to shareholders, including $93M in share repurchases, representing a 14% shareholder return yield Second Quarter 2026 Results Average production: 1,253 MMcfepd (209 Mboepd) Production exit rate (a) : 1,275 MMcfepd (213 Mboepd) Total Commodity Revenue : $504M Net Income: $248M, inclusive of gain on non-cash unsettled derivatives Adjusted EBITDA (b) : $240M Operating Cash Flow: $89M Adjusted Free Cash Flow (c) : $115M Capital Expenditures: $40M Rusty Hutson, Jr., CEO of Diversified, commented: "The Diversified team delivered another quarter of strong operational and financial performance, while maintaining our disciplined approach to capital allocation. Importantly, we ended the quarter with leverage within our targeted range and substantial liquidity available for deployment into future value generating opportunities, underscoring the resilience of our asset base and the consistency of our portfolio's cash-generating capabilities. As we look ahead, Diversified is entering a compelling new phase of growth. The successful integration of the Canvas and Sheridan acquisitions, along with the closing of the Camino transaction have further enhanced the scale, quality, and inventory depth of our portfolio, strengthening our position as a leading owner and operator of long-life energy assets. At the same time, we are expanding our value creation playbook through the introduction of a disciplined operated development program in Oklahoma. Our focus within this expansive set of development opportunities in Oklahoma is to add future reserves and new production, which we expect will enhance and grow our cash flow. With our new operated development program, we are complementing the success of our non-operated development partnerships, portfolio optimization initiatives, and strategic infrastructure investments to grow cash flow. These complementary growth platforms provide greater flexibility in how we allocate capital, create shareholder value, and drive sustainable production and cash flow performance. With a premier acreage position, an extensive inventory of highly economic development opportunities, and multiple pathways to generate attractive returns, we are increasingly able to control our growth profile while reducing reliance on acquisitions alone to sustain long-term performance. We have never been better positioned to deliver durable cash flow, create long-term shareholder value, and build the foundation for the next 25 years of growth." Expanded significant Oklahoma footprint: Estimated more than 450 economic drilling locations at $65/Bbl oil and $3.25/MMBtu natural gas pricing, representing over 20 years of development runway at a one-rig pace. This inventory provides strong visibility into future production, reserves, and cash flow generation. Experienced execution team : Led by Chief Operating Officer Rick Gideon and internal development team. Leveraging acreage acquired primarily through PDP-focused transactions, DEC is positioned to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns through a measured, capital-disciplined development program that adds to Diversified's already resilient and proven cash generating capabilities. Proven operations platform: Supported by Smarter Asset Management practices, a vertically integrated operating platform, and technology-enabled field operations, our strategy can be executed within a low-cost framework. Non-Operated Development Platform Provides a Meaningful Driver of Capital-Efficient Growth Non-operated value creation : Serves as an important component of our strategy to unlock cash flow, providing capital-efficient production growth and attractive returns through partnerships with leading operators. Strategic partnerships: Continental Resources, Mewbourne, and a private Northwest Shelf operator provide diversified, capital-efficient exposure to high-return development opportunities across multiple core basins. Incremental production addition: Expected to offset approximately 50% of the Company's portfolio production decline, representing an estimated average contribution of approximately 12,500 Boepd during 2026. By combining operated and non-operated development opportunities with our proven acquisition and asset management expertise, Diversified has built a durable growth platform, capable of generating long-term shareholder value across commodity cycles. Unlocking Value Through Portfolio Optimization: Strategic Divestitures Enhance Asset Quality and Financial Flexibility Sale of non-core Barnett Shale and Arkansas assets: Represents another successful step in Diversified's Portfolio Optimization Program ("POP"), which is focused on high-grading the asset base, improving margins, enhancing liquidity, and reallocating capital toward higher-return opportunities. Since the beginning of 2023, Diversified has generated more than $500 million through acreage sales and asset divestitures, demonstrating the value and optionality embedded within our expansive portfolio. Barnett Shale assets sale: Generated approximately $130 million in gross proceeds. The divested assets produced approximately 52 MMcfe/d and contributed approximately $13 million of annual EBITDA. The transaction added approximately $47 million of liquidity post fees, debt repayment, and hedge book termination and is expected to improve margins across our Central Region through the disposition of higher-cost production. Sale of certain Arkansas assets: Generated approximately $17 million in gross proceeds. These assets produced approximately 2 MMcfe/d and contributed approximately $2 million of annual EBITDA. These recent transactions further sharpen our operational focus while reinforcing our commitment to disciplined capital allocation. Collectively, we will continue to evaluate and high-grade our assets from our vast portfolio optimization program opportunities that enhance the durability of our business model and support DEC's evolution into a premier U.S. energy producer focused on creating long-term shareholder value. The Company's production volume mix was approximately 71% natural gas, 15% NGL's, and 14% oil. title: Genasys Receives Follow-On $2.4M LRAD CIP Order
summary: Remotely operated LRAD systems providing surveillance and first response capabilities for large U.S. utility company's substations
body_text: LRAD 950NXTs Providing Large U.S. Utility Substations Remotely Operated Surveillance and First Response Capabilities SAN DIEGO, CA – August 5, 2026 – Genasys Inc. (NASDAQ: GNSS), the global leader in Protective Communications ®, today announced a new $2.4 million critical infrastructure protection (CIP) order for one of the nation’s largest utility companies. The order follows the recent installation of LRAD ® 950NXT systems at one of the utility’s major substations, and a subsequent $2.0 million order to outfit additional substations with the remotely operated LRADs. The 950XTs will be fully integrated with the substations’ existing physical security and include multi-sensor perimeter intrusion detection from integration partner, iEnet. “More and more critical infrastructure operators around the world are trusting Genasys systems and solutions to safeguard vital assets and protect people,” said Genasys CEO Richard Danforth. “The unparalleled surveillance, first response, and on-site intervention capabilities of our LRAD 950NXTs are being deployed by utilities, dams, ports, nuclear energy facilities, power plants, data centers, and other essential infrastructure.” Sensor-integrated 950NXTs elevate and enhance CIP by turning passive monitoring into immediate security threat responses and interventions. LRAD 950NXT systems fully address the North American Electric Reliability Corporation’s physical security requirements to Detect, Assess, Communicate, Respond, Delay, and Deter electrical transmission and distribution asset threats. About Genasys Inc. Genasys is the global leader in Protective Communications®, providing the most comprehensive portfolio of preparedness, response, and analytics software and hardware solutions available. The company’s Long Range Acoustic Device® (LRAD®) and Protect Platform, which includes Genasys Protect® and Genasys Evertel®, are designed around one premise: ensuring organizations and public safety agencies are Ready when it matters ®. Protecting people and saving lives for over 40 years, Genasys covers more than 155 million people in all 50 states and in over 100 countries worldwide. For more information, visit genasys.com . title: How McCoy's Building Supply Stayed Family-Owned in a Rolled-Up Trade
summary: McCoy's Building Supply ranks BM #19 on MDM's 2026 Top Distributors list. How a fourth-generation Texas family kept it after Home Depot nearly ended it.
body_text: Part of Distributor Playbooks — strategy teardowns of every company on the MDM Top Distributors lists . New to the 2026 lists. McCoy's Building Supply lands at BM #19 on MDM's 2026 Top Distributors list , the annual ranking from Modern Distribution Management of North America's largest wholesale distributors, with $1.2 billion in revenue across 85 stores in Texas, Oklahoma and New Mexico. That number alone doesn't explain much. What makes McCoy's worth studying is who still owns it: the same family that started it in Galveston in 1927, four generations later, in a sector where nearly every peer of comparable size has been bought by private equity or a public roll-up. A roofing crew that became a lumberyard Frank McCoy started as a contract roofer, moving the business from Houston to Galveston in 1927. It was his son Emmett who turned it into something else. After World War II, Emmett saw homeowners wanting to buy materials and do the work themselves, and in the 1940s he launched McCoy Supply Company to sell roofing and building materials directly to the public. He kept the roofing crews running alongside the new retail arm until 1964, when he dropped contract roofing entirely, added lumber, and turned the operation into what became McCoy's Building Supply Centers. The company's founding test came in 1961, when Hurricane Carla tore through the Texas Gulf Coast. Materials suppliers across the region raised prices on desperate homeowners. Emmett didn't. That decision, according to Family Business Magazine , built the community trust that carried McCoy's through the rebuilding boom and pushed the company past $1 million in annual sales for the first time. It's a small episode, but it set a pattern the company still points to: hold the line on price discipline as a long-game asset, not a short-term lever. The near-death nobody puts on the About page By the mid-1970s, Emmett's three sons, Michael, Brian and Dennis, had joined the business and were driving an expansion that eventually topped 100 locations. Then, in 1985, Dennis McCoy died in a plane crash at 28, flying to a store location. Mike and Brian, the surviving brothers, restructured leadership around the loss and kept building. The real threat came a decade later. When Home Depot and Lowe's pushed into Texas in the mid-1990s, McCoy's lost roughly half its revenue within two years and had to close 29 of its 110 stores. For a regional lumberyard chain built on relationships and delivery trucks, big-box retail with national buying power was close to an extinction event. McCoy's survived it, but the strain reshaped the company. In 2000, Mike McCoy wanted to sell. The family split: Brian's branch bought the operating company in 2001 and leased facilities back from the extended family, while Mike retired after three decades running the business. It is the kind of internal fracture most "family legacy" narratives smooth over, but it's the hinge on which the modern McCoy's turns. What survived on the other side wasn't a united family conglomerate. It was one branch of the family, committed to running the company as an operator rather than a portfolio asset, at the exact moment competitors with deeper pockets were arriving in force. Why this matters more now than it did then That distinction is the piece's unique insight. Building materials distribution in North America has consolidated hard over the past fifteen years. Builders FirstSource and BMC merged into a public giant. US LBM rolled up dozens of regional yards under a private-equity sponsor before going public. Foundation Building Materials, SRS Distribution and a long list of others have changed hands between PE firms multiple times. Against that backdrop, an $1.2 billion, 85-store chain that is still privately held by descendants of the founder, with no PE sponsor and no public filing requirement, is the outlier, not the norm. McCoy's paid for that independence with a slower, in-house-everything model rather than acquisition-fueled scale. The company runs its own commercial credit program alongside a Synchrony-backed private-label card, rather than outsourcing contractor financing. It operates its own delivery fleet, a detail the company still markets in its green-and-yellow trucks, and by 2000 had already grown that fleet past 300 vehicles to guarantee same-day jobsite delivery. It built two millworks facilities and two distribution centers rather than relying purely on vendor drop-ship. And it diversified into farm and ranch equipment, a category adjacency that gives McCoy's a customer base independent of new-home construction cycles, useful insulation when residential building slows. The generational handoff, and the current bet Brian McCoy stepped down as CEO in 2022 after roughly two decades in the role, becoming board chairman. His daughter, Meagan McCoy Jones, became the company's first woman president and CEO, the fourth generation to lead it. Under her, McCoy's has kept expanding rather than consolidating defensively: a new store opened in New Caney, Texas in spring 2026, and the company closed the Rio Truss acquisition in December 2024, adding structural component manufacturing in the Rio Grande Valley, per the company's press release and trade coverage in LBM Journal . It also closed a store in Plainview in early 2026, a reminder that staying private doesn't mean staying static. The bet embedded in all of it is that a family that has already turned down a sale once, survived a big-box invasion, and split apart and reformed around a single operating branch, is better positioned to make patient, decades-long capital calls than a sponsor working a five-to-seven-year hold. Whether that holds as the next generation takes the wheel is the open question worth watching. Distribution is won in unglamorous places: the branch that stays open through a storm, the truck that shows up same-day, the catalog kept current enough that a contractor never has to call twice. McCoy's has spent a century proving that ownership structure is one more variable a distributor gets to choose.

title: 8 email prospecting tools for faster pipeline
summary: Compare the best email prospecting tools. We cover features, pricing, and ideal use cases for Artisan, ZoomInfo, Instantly, Lemlist, and more.
body_text: Building a prospecting stack too often means signing annual contracts and hoping that data quality, email deliverability, and outreach personalization hold up. We’ve curated this list based on what B2B sales teams actually use and recommend. The eight tools below cover every vertical in the category, from all-in-one platforms to dedicated database providers and CRM-native solutions. How to choose an email prospecting tool Prospecting tools generally fall into one of two categories: all-in-one solutions and point solutions. Whether you opt for a consolidated platform will depend on your feature needs, compliance requirements, and, of course, budget. Use the following criteria when comparing vendors: Database size and data freshness: Check the vendor's B2B data coverage in your target regions and ask for bounce rates in your specific segment, especially outside the US. Deliverability infrastructure: Look for automatic domain warm-up, mailbox rotation, real-time bounce detection, and spam complaint monitoring across major providers. Personalization depth: AI-powered personalization that references prospect activity is the best means of scaling tailored outreach. Intent data and buyer signals: Ask which signals the vendor tracks (first-party website activity, content consumption, G2 activity, job changes, funding events) and how they appear inside your workflow. Compliance: This is non-negotiable for European prospecting, so look for GDPR-compliant data collection, automatic suppression of opted-out contacts, and EU data residency options. CRM integration: If the vendor doesn't include a built-in CRM, confirm native two-way sync with yours, as support beyond Salesforce and HubSpot varies by platform. Pricing model: Compare per-seat, per-credit, unlimited sending, and enterprise contracts based on your team size, volume, and compliance needs. The best email prospecting tools at a glance Tool Category Best for Strength Starting price Artisan All-in-one prospecting solution SDR teams running high-volume outbound AI-powered personalization and autonomous campaigns Flexible pricing based on outreach needs; see pricing page Apollo All-in-one prospecting solution Early-stage and mid-market teams new to outbound Broad database with built-in sequencing $59/month Saleshandy All-in-one prospecting solution SMB teams running high-volume cold email Deliverability optimization and unlimited email accounts $36/month ZoomInfo Database and enrichment Enterprise teams running ABM or high-ACV deals Firmographic, technographic, and intent data depth Custom Cognism Database and enrichment Teams prospecting into UK and EMEA markets Phone-verified mobiles with GDPR compliance built in $14,000/year Lusha Database and enrichment Individual reps needing fast LinkedIn contact lookups One-click email and direct dial from LinkedIn $49.99/month HubSpot Sales Hub Sales workflows Teams already on HubSpot wanting native sequencing Prospecting and outreach native to the CRM $10/month Pipedrive Sales workflows SMBs wanting simple pipeline management Clean UI with over 400 integrations $24/month Best all-in-one email prospecting platforms If you're building an outbound motion from scratch, all-in-one platforms are worth evaluating first. These tools combine a lead database, email discovery, sequence automation, and analytics in a single solution. 1. Artisan Artisan is an AI-powered sales platform built around Ava, an AI BDR that handles prospect research, outreach personalization, and sequence management without manual input. Key features Access to over 250 million verified contacts with filters for job title, industry, company size, and intent signals Fill profile enrichment (including email and phone numbers) Website visitor tracking AI-powered outreach personalization that pulls from social media activity, funding announcements, job postings, and company news Automated sequence management across email and social media Autonomous replies and meeting booking AI-powered A/B testing Built-in email warm-up, domain rotation, and deliverability monitoring Native two-way sync with Salesforce and HubSpot Who is Artisan best for? Artisan works best for large sales development representative (SDR) teams running outbound at scale. It's also a strong fit for early-stage companies that want to cover prospecting without hiring a full SDR team. Teams running highly customized, relationship-driven outreach to very small prospect lists will need more fine-tuning for an AI SDR to match their voice. Pricing Artisan has several usage-based plans for different user needs and outreach requirements. A free plan is also available to explore the platform. You can see a full breakdown on the pricing page . 2. Apollo.io Apollo.io is a sales intelligence and engagement platform. It combines prospect search, email sequencing, and basic CRM functionality in a single solution. Key features Access to over 230 million verified contacts Email sequencing with A/B testing and automated follow-ups LinkedIn prospecting via Chrome extension Built-in dialer for phone outreach AI-assisted email writing with basic personalization Email deliverability guardrails Native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Pipedrive Conversation intelligence based on analysis of recorded calls Who is Apollo best for? Apollo fits early-stage and mid-market sales teams that need a broad contact database and basic sequence automation without a complex setup. It's a strong starting point for teams that are new to outbound and want one tool to cover prospecting, outreach, and light CRM functionality. However, teams running personalized outreach at scale will hit the ceiling on Apollo's email writing capabilities quickly. Pricing (Paid Monthly) Basic: $65/month/user (2500 credits) Professional: $99/month/user (4000 credits) Organization (min. 3 users): $149/month/user (6000 credits) Apollo offers a free plan with limited credits and basic features. 3. Saleshandy Saleshandy is a cold email outreach platform focused on high-volume sequence automation and deliverability optimization. Key features Multi-sender rotation across unlimited connected email accounts Unified inbox for reply management across all connected accounts Built-in email address verifier and inbox placement testing Native B2B lead finder with 852 million contacts (sold separately) AI-powered email campaigns Multivariate testing Native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Pipedrive, and Zoho Who is Saleshandy best for? Saleshandy's team-based pricing has dramatically lower costs than per-user competitors. That makes it an affordable option for small to mid-sized SDR teams running high-volume cold email campaigns. Agencies also often choose Salesfandy for unlimited email accounts. Pricing (Paid Monthly) Saleshandy offers two categories of plans: its Outreach packages for email outreach automation and its Lead packages for prospecting. There are also various add-ons, such as a dialer and native CRM, available. Outreach Starter: $36/month (6,000 monthly emails) Outreach Pro: $99/month (150,000 monthly emails) Outreach Scale: $199/month (240,000 monthly emails) Lead Starter: $59/month (2,500 credits per month) Lead Pro: $99/month (4000 credits per month) Unlimited email account connections are included across every tier. The lead finder credits included in the Outreach plans (50 on Starter, 100 on Pro and Scale) reset monthly but cover very little volume at scale. If you're planning to use Saleshandy as your primary prospecting source, budget for a Lead subscription or a separate database on top of the base cost. Best lead database and enrichment tools If you already have an outreach tool you're happy with, these dedicated data providers will complete your sales toolkit with verified contact data. They focus on verified contact and company data that feeds directly into your outreach tool or CRM. 4. ZoomInfo ZoomInfo is a data platform that provides deep contact and company intelligence. It's one of the largest B2B databases on the market, with particularly extensive coverage of US mid-market and enterprise companies. Key features 420 million contact profiles and 145 million company profiles, with 120 million verified phone numbers In-depth technographic data, including tech stack, software installs, and cloud infrastructure Intent data covering regulatory filings, real-time org chart changes, executive moves, and website visitor activity Org chart mapping for identifying buying committees and navigating complex accounts Native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Snowflake via GTM Studio AI-powered account scoring and prioritization through ZoomInfo Copilot Who is ZoomInfo best for? ZoomInfo makes sense for enterprise teams selling high-value deals to a defined list of target accounts. It's harder to justify for smaller teams, high-volume prospecting motions, or anyone selling primarily outside North America (data accuracy drops off noticeably in EMEA and APAC). Pricing ZoomInfo doesn’t publish its pricing. 5. Cognism Cognism is a B2B sales intelligence platform with a focus on GDPR-compliant contact data and phone-verified mobile numbers. Key features Global contact database with the strongest coverage across the UK, DACH, and Nordic regions Manually phone-verified mobile numbers with reported connect rates 2 to 3 times higher than standard databases Do not call list screening across 15 countries Intent data via Bombora integration Chrome extension for pulling verified contact data directly from LinkedIn profiles Native integrations with Salesforce, HubSpot, Salesloft, and Outreach Who is Cognism best for? Due to mobile data quality and GDPR compliance deeply embedded in the product, Cognism is a go-to for SDR teams doing high-volume cold calling to the UK and European markets. Pricing Cognism’s pricing starts at $14,000/year for pure lead discovery and list-building functionality. CRM enrichment can be layered as an add-on. At $18,750/year, on-demand data validation is available. 6. Lusha Lusha is a prospecting and enrichment tool that is well-known for its Chrome extension that lets sales reps pull verified emails and direct dials from LinkedIn profiles with a single click. Key features Access to a prospecting database with 30M company profiles Ongoing CRM data enrichment Chrome extension for instant email and direct dial lookups from LinkedIn profiles and company websites CRM push to Salesforce and HubSpot directly from the extension Bulk enrichment and CSV upload for list-level data enrichment Intent signals, job change alerts, and technographic filters on higher-tier plans Who is Lusha best for? Lusha works well for individual reps or small businesses who need quick contact information. If your prospecting workflow is LinkedIn-heavy and you want to find phone numbers and verified emails without leaving your browser, Lusha is a good option. That said, Lusha doesn't offer the same compliance infrastructure as Cognism, which makes it less suitable for prospecting in regulated European markets. Pricing (Paid MOnthly) Lusha’s free plan includes 40 credits per month. A custom enterprise plan is available. Starter: $49.90/month (400 credits/month, 1 seat) Pro: $69.90/month (600 credits/month, 2 seats) Premium: $399.90/month (3,400 credits/month, 5 seats) Best CRM-integrated prospecting tools For teams that live in their CRM, adding a separate prospecting tool creates sync issues and extra overhead. These platforms eliminate the need for manual imports by offering in-house prospecting alongside their core CRM or integrating easily with multiple providers. 7. HubSpot Sales Hub HubSpot Sales Hub is the sales layer of HubSpot's CRM platform, combining email sequences, templates, meeting scheduling, and contact management in a single environment. Its Breeze Prospecting Agent monitors accounts already in your CRM for buying signals and alerts reps when they’re ready for timely outreach. Key features Integrates with third-party providers like ZoomInfo, Apollo, and Surfe to surface target accounts and their contact details Proprietary Breeze Prospecting Agent monitors enrolled accounts for buying signals Email sequences with automated follow-ups Meeting scheduling with calendar sync Breeze Intelligence, an AI prospecting agent Built-in deal pipeline, forecasting, and custom reporting Native integrations with over 1,700 tools Who is HubSpot Sales Hub best for? HubSpot Sales Hub makes the most sense for teams already running on HubSpot CRM who want native sequencing and AI-assisted outreach without adding external tools. Pricing Breeze Prospecting Agent is available on all Sales Hub plans. It consumes 1000 credits for every lead it puts forward for outreach. A limited free plan is available. Starter: $10/month/seat (500 credits) Professional: $100/month/seat (3000 credits) Enterprise: $150/month/seat (5000 credits) 8. Pipedrive Pipedrive is a simple CRM designed for frictionless deal management. Its prospecting tool is called LeadBooster and includes an AI chatbot for website visitors and access to a large database. Key features Built-in lead generation tool with live chat, chatbot, web forms, and meeting scheduler via LeadBooster Database of over 400 million profiles via Leadbooster Visual pipeline with customizable deal stages and activity tracking Two-way email sync with open and click tracking Workflow automation for deal movement and activity creation Meeting scheduler with calendar sync Native integrations with Gmail, Outlook, Slack, and over 400 third-party tools Who is Pipedrive best for? Pipedrive suits SMBs that want a clean, easy-to-use pipeline tool and don't need the complexity of HubSpot. Pricing To access prospecting tools, you’ll need to purchase a base plan and include Leadbooster as an add-on for $39/month. Lite: $24/user/month Growth: $49/user/month Premium: $79/user/month Ultimate: $99/user/month Fewer tools, faster pipeline One of the core decisions you will make as you look for a prospecting tool is whether to consolidate into one platform or build a stack of specialized tools. Dedicated database providers give you deeper data coverage in specific regions or verticals, but they require a separate sequencing tool, a separate deliverability layer, and someone to keep everything in sync. The overhead of managing three or four vendors increases fast, and so do the data hygiene problems. If you want one platform that handles prospecting, outreach, and deliverability without building a stack, Artisan combines a 250M-strong contact database, intent monitoring, AI-generated outreach, and built-in email infrastructure in a single product. All of which gives your team more time to focus on closing deals. Automate your outbound with an AI BDR Meet Ava—your AI BDR who handles prospecting, outreach, and follow-ups, so your team can focus on closing.

title: Building Lasting Partnerships in Freight: Troy Shasko on Relationships, Service and Staying Driven
summary: In our latest Landstar agent profile, Troy Shasko shares how experience, integrity, discipline and a relationship-first mindset have shaped his approach for decades.
body_text: In the Landstar network, success is often built over time—through relationships, consistency and a commitment to doing the right thing. For Troy Shasko, that mindset has helped shape a long-standing independent Landstar agency focused on customer trust, operational strength and enduring partnerships across North America. With decades in the business, Shasko has grown his family-based agency by combining hands-on industry experience with an entrepreneurial drive, emphasizing accountability, communication and service at every step. In this Landstar agent profile, you’ll learn: Why long-term relationships are central to sustained growth How Landstar’s network supports expansion across modes and markets What it takes to build a reputation rooted in service and consistency Why an entrepreneurial mindset still matters—no matter how long you’ve been in the business Building capabilities through long-term relationships Based in Belle Vernon, Pennsylvania, Shasko Team Logistics has built a reputation for delivering transportation solutions with some of the most respected names in retail, manufacturing, energy, and heavy haul project logistics for decades. Since joining the family business in 1986, Troy Shasko has helped grow an agency that has been part of the Landstar network since its early years. Today, the agency supports customers across multiple modes, including contract truckload, hazmat, heavy haul, cross-border freight (Mexico and Canada) and time-sensitive shipments, with a significant portion of the business focused on high-value contract freight and heavy haul project logistics, with an emphasis on delivering consistent service and maintaining long-term customer relationships. Shasko’s project logistics experience includes planning and coordinating complex, multi-phase transportation programs for large-scale construction and industrial projects. Building the foundation: experience, integrity and follow-through From his early days working on loading docks to serving as a U.S. Army logistics and aviation officer, Shasko developed a practical understanding of freight and operations before entering the agency business. That foundation helped shape a straightforward approach to business: Do the right thing Follow through on commitments Treat customers and operators with respect and care Over time, that approach has helped foster long-term relationships with customers who have worked with the agency for years. For Shasko, that consistency starts with a simple leadership principle: “Be a great team player and lead your team.” What helped most: leveraging the Landstar network and relationships As the agency grew, Shasko emphasized the importance of working closely with both Landstar’s corporate resources and network of owner-operators. Doing so helped build capacity and allowed the agency to pursue new opportunities in complex modes and services. And, over time, that collaboration has led to his agency’s reputation for consistent service, with some operators supporting specific lanes for many years. The combination of relationships, tools and network support has helped his agency deliver the safety, security and service customers expect. For one year-long project, Shasko’s team helped coordinate more than 3,300 truckload shipments, including more than 1,100 over-dimensional heavy haul truckloads, along with expedited, LTL, ocean and air shipments moving from multiple U.S. states and international origins. The agency’s support helped the team complete the project both on time and on budget. Think like an owner: the mindset behind long-term success For Shasko, success comes back to mentality. He emphasizes the importance of staying driven and continually earning your place on the team. “I fire myself at the end of every day and work to improve and earn my position back the next day” he says—a reflection of the entrepreneurial mindset that continues to guide the agency. His advice for new agents Be driven. Approach each day with urgency and accountability. Do the right thing. Integrity and follow-through build long-term trust. Hustle daily. Engage with every opportunity and learn the business. Build relationships . Strong connections with customers, owner-operators and corporate teams support growth. FAQ: Becoming a Landstar Freight Agent 1. What does a Landstar freight agent do? A Landstar freight agent is an independent business owner who builds customer relationships and arranges transportation solutions while leveraging the Landstar network and resources to help move freight and communicate the results quickly. 2. How does Landstar support freight agents? Support includes access to technology, operations and an established capacity network that helps agents meet customer needs and expand capabilities. 3. What advice does Shasko give for long-term success as an agent? For Shasko, long-term success comes from consistency, relationship-building, follow-through and a strong work ethic rooted in discipline and integrity. He points to a Lou Holtz quote as a reminder of the mindset required to sustain success: “Ability is what you’re capable of doing. Motivation determines what you do. Attitude determines how well you do it.”
